about: InterCat's content fixture decoder at version 1 (contracts/content-v1.md §4): each case a message InterCat's content fixture sent, its bytes one character each, U+0000 to U+00FF, kept up to its record limit, and the decoding version 1 makes of what was kept. A decoder that decodes any case otherwise is another version, with a corpus of its own (contracts/decoders-v1.md §3a).

cases.name: a whole text message
cases.message: InterCat content fixture message 7 on conversation 2. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
fields: the fixture's filler sentence, repeated (45 bytes)

cases.name: a message cut by its record limit
cases.message: InterCat content fixture message 7 on conversation 2. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
fields: the fixture's filler sentence, repeated (10 bytes)
cases.notDecoded: The capture kept the first 64 of the message's 144 bytes; the rest was never kept, so it is not decoded.

cases.name: a message whose number the cut leaves unended
cases.notDecoded: The message ends inside the fixture's header, at byte 33, so it names no more than the fields decoded.

cases.name: a message that is not the fixture's
cases.notDecoded: At byte 0 it leaves the header a fixture text message begins with, so it carries no fields the decoder reads; the fixture's byte messages are bytes alone.

cases.name: a message whose filler breaks
cases.message: InterCat content fixture message 3 on conversation 1. The quick brown cat.
fields: 21 bytes, which leave the fixture's filler sentence at byte 70
